new_scholarship.name: Horatio Alger Association National Scholarship
new_scholarship.program_type: Need-based scholarship from a non-governmental organisation
new_scholarship.official_source: Horatio Alger Association of Distinguished Americans
new_scholarship.description: The Horatio Alger Association of Distinguished Americans, a 501(c)(3) educational nonprofit headquartered in Alexandria, Virginia, awards 105 National Scholarships of USD 25,000 each to high school juniors across all 50 states and Washington DC who intend to complete a bachelor's degree. Eligibility is explicitly need-based: applicants must have an adjusted gross family income of USD 100,000 or lower. Applicants must also show integrity and perseverance in overcoming adversity, be involved in co-curricular and community service, and maintain a minimum GPA of 2.0. One application is considered for all scholarships for which the applicant is eligible. Admission to college is separate: the award does not include admission to any institution.
new_scholarship.funding_period: per award over the course of the bachelor's degree
new_scholarship.duration: Four-year undergraduate scholarship supporting a bachelor's degree
new_scholarship.deadline: Junior application period: December 1 - March 1; Senior application period: December 1 - February 15
new_scholarship.application_period: Opens December 1 and closes March 1 for high school juniors; opens December 1 and closes February 15 for high school seniors. As of 2026-10-04 the next cycle opens on December 1, 2026.
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Enrolled full time as a high school junior in the United States, committed to completing a bachelor's degree immediately after high school at an accredited non-profit public or private US institution (a two-year start followed by transfer is allowed), with an adjusted gross family income of USD 100,000 or lower, a minimum GPA of 2.0, co-curricular and community service involvement, and demonstrated integrity and perseverance in overcoming adversity. Must be a United States citizen.

new_scholarship.selection_notes: The Association states that while most other scholarships focus exclusively on academic achievement or leadership potential, Horatio Alger Scholarships are also intended for promising students who have critical financial need, demonstrate integrity and perseverance in overcoming adversity, and are determined to succeed. Some member-funded specialized scholarships require a separate application; the National Scholarship is awarded through the single general application.

new_scholarship.notes: The National Scholarship is one of over 70 scholarship programmes administered by the Association, which awards 105 National Scholarships each cycle. Other member-funded and state-restricted awards, such as the Bergeron Everglades Environmental Steward Scholarship for Florida residents studying environmental sciences or the Denny Sanford institutional awards, are separate applications with their own eligibility rules.

new_scholarship.name: Building Brighter Futures: Bursaries and Scholarships (Indspire)
new_scholarship.program_type: Indigenous student bursary and scholarship programme (charitable fund)
new_scholarship.description: Indspire, a national Indigenous registered charity, runs Building Brighter Futures, a bursary and scholarship programme for First Nations, Inuit and Métis students in Canada. One application is used for all Indspire bursaries and scholarships, with only a few named exceptions requiring a separate application. The funding model is deliberately unrestricted: Indspire states that wherever possible funds are awarded to a student to use as they wish, for tuition, childcare, food, cultural support, shelter or travel. Applications for the September 2026 to August 2027 academic year are accepted with deadlines on August 1, November 1 and February 1 at 11:59 p.m. EST, so the programme is accepting applications on 2026-10-04 with the next deadline on 1 November 2026.

new_scholarship.program_type: Need-based scholarship from a non-governmental organisation
new_scholarship.description: The Etta Gray Memorial Scholarship Program, administered by the United Negro College Fund, provides a one-time USD 5,000 need-based scholarship award to students who have a permanent residence in upstate South Carolina and who are pursuing a technical certification at a two-year or four-year college or university in Upstate South Carolina. It was established in honour of the memory of Etta Gray, a loving caregiver for the William Hipp family. UNCF describes itself as the nation's largest private scholarship provider to minority group members and states it awards more than USD 62 million in scholarships each year to students at more than 600 schools. The programme is open on 2026-10-04 with a published deadline of October 30.

new_scholarship.name: Frederick Douglass Bicentennial Scholarship Program (UNCF)
new_scholarship.program_type: Need-based scholarship for HBCU students, administered by a non-governmental organisation
new_scholarship.description: The Frederick Douglass Bicentennial Scholarship Program was established by Tony Signore and funded by the Signore Family to support students attending accredited historically black colleges and universities nationwide. UNCF administers and manages the programme for 20 years, through academic year 2038-39. Each year the programme awards two USD 10,000 scholarships to exceptional HBCU seniors who have demonstrated high academic achievement, strong leadership skills, a commitment to community service and unmet financial need. Applicants must hold a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.5 on a 4.0 scale and must complete a Free Application for Federal Student Aid. The programme is recurring and the next application session has not yet opened on the official page.
